newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bond spreads outperform dollar bloc.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bond spreads outperform dollar bloc.

text.p: Australian bonds outperformed their dollar-bloc counterparts on Monday, with spreads on long bonds closing at their narrowest since the surprise half percent rate cut last Wednesday.
In a day of trading dominated by the rollover of the expiring December bond futures, long bonds led the way with the curves reversing some of last week's steepening.
Local bonds gained most against Canadian bonds, which ended last week on a softer note, and New Zealand bonds, where the market is waiting on Tuesday's Reserve Bank monetary policy statement.

But bonds were also firmer against the U.S. which continued their stronger tone of last week into Tokyo trading, with the long bond touching under 100 points and closing regaining almost all of Thursday and Friday's widening.
Traders said a bid tone, noticeably at the long end, kept the market firm and saw the local yield curve flatten.
However, despite the flattening, the curves are much steeper than those ahead of last week's rate cut.

Economists said a spread of 70 points, which was as steep as the curve was getting before the cut, was now likely to be its flattest point over coming months, while a yield curve spread of over 100 points was possible.

"Almost all of the 50 basis point rate cut has built into a steeper 3-10 year yield spread and periodic long end weakness may steepen the curve further, conceivably out to 110 basis points," UBS Australia chief economist Stephen Roberts said.
